headline: Apple prototyped a shorter Apple Pencil for foldable iPhone, but launch is 'unlikely'.
summary: According to Mark Gurman, a 'stubbier' Apple Pencil was tested for the upcoming foldable iPhone, but design challenges and screen fragility make its release improbable.
details: Apple has internally prototyped a 'stubbier' Apple Pencil designed for its upcoming foldable iPhone, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. However, Gurman noted that it is 'unlikely' this accessory will launch alongside the first foldable iPhone.

The prototype stylus would attach magnetically to the side for storage and charging, similar to existing Apple Pencils. This attachment point could interfere with the foldable display when opened, and styluses risk marking delicate foldable screens.

Gurman also reported on a significant Apple Watch overhaul, including testing white and dark gray ceramic cases for the Series 12. A new feature for continuous heart-rate monitoring throughout the day is also being tested.

Additionally, Apple is reportedly revamping its fitness and health app to resemble platforms like Whoop and Oura. A major redesign for the Apple Watch is anticipated for 2027, with a potential delay to 2028.

headline_marked: [[Google Maps now shows ‘Lake America’]] instead of Lake Ontario for US users
headline: Google Maps now shows ‘Lake America’ instead of Lake Ontario for US users
summary: Google adopted the new name for US users following a presidential executive order, part of an ongoing trade dispute with Canada. Canadian users will still see "Lake Ontario".
details: Google Maps has updated the name of Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' for users in the United States. This change follows a presidential executive order issued days prior, which mandated the rebranding of the Great Lake in official government databases.

The executive order is reportedly part of an ongoing trade dispute with Canada, whose capital province is named Ontario. A similar order in January 2025 renamed the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, which other map providers also adopted.

While Apple Maps and Bing Maps have not yet reflected 'Lake America,' they are expected to follow suit as the federal government's Geographic Names Information System database updates. Google states its policy is to show country-specific names for bodies of water.
Consequently, users in the US will see 'Lake America,' while those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario.' Users outside both countries will see both names displayed.

The move has sparked debate in open-source mapping communities like OpenStreetMap, which offers organizations the choice of which name to display. However, MapQuest has publicly stated it will not adopt the change.
